Each button plays an existing recording from the revised script. The game uses the same exact-line matches; narration, choices and receipts are not read as a character’s dialogue.

The dramatic spine

The ordinary promise is to return a reed case to Mara. Nell’s father gives Sable someone he can save before the mystery gives him something he wants. His mother’s copied song ties his grief to a public wrong. The Crown’s fall is a real victory, but the later chapters reveal the harm it leaves behind and the crew’s own part in it. The last act asks them to make room for living people to answer, rather than impose one perfect song. The journey ends by returning to the home and promise with which it began.
